messages:
Alex K: FYI — BillCheckr sent their final quote for the usage analytics pilot. putting this here for procurement + finance review. key points: committed 500k tokens/mo, 12‑month term, 15% volume discount, $5k onboarding fee. quote link: https://vendor-quotes.internal/billcheckr/17688
Maria P: thanks alex. can you paste the per-unit math? also need to know invoice cadence and whether they accept PO vs invoice with net-30.
Alex K: sure — copied the relevant lines from the quote:
```
Tier           | Monthly tokens | Unit price / 1M tokens | Monthly $ (est)
---------------|----------------|------------------------|-----------------
Committed      | 500,000        | $20                   | $10,000
Overage        | variable       | $25                   | depends
One-time       | onboarding     | —                     | $5,000
Estimated TCV  | 12 months      | —                     | $125,000 (w/15%)
```
They listed monthly invoicing, prefer annual prepay for the 15% tier but said will accept monthly invoice with TCV noted.
Elaine (Fin): need final per-1M token price as a single number for our GL mapping and to run against forecast. also confirm whether tax is included and who is responsible for EU VAT. we can't approve until we have invoice cadence + billing entity.
Alex K: copied again — per-1M = $20 on committed volume, $25 for overages. tax excluded, vendor will bill from US entity.
Maria P: i'll ask them to: 1) confirm billing entity and VAT handling, 2) accept PO (we prefer PO/net-30), 3) provide SOC2 report and DPA. can we push for a shorter term for the pilot? 12 months is long. recommend 6 months with a 30-day opt-out after month 3.
James P: quick product ask — does their usage meter match our token counting? if they meter differently we could get mismatches in billing. alex, did they share metering spec or sample event payloads?
Alex K: not yet, asked for metering spec in my reply. vendor said they use token counts based on the same tokenizer but haven't shared schema. i'll request sample logs.
procure-bot: Reminder — vendor approvals need budget code and PO request in #procurement-requests before legal review. use template: /po create <vendor> <amount> <budget-code>.
Elaine (Fin): rough go/no-go from finance: if TCV <= $140k and they accept PO/net-30 and provide SOC2 + DPA, finance is OK to proceed. onboarding fee needs to be waived or credited in first invoice.
Maria P: negotiating plan: ask for 6-month pilot, waive onboarding, 20% discount for 6-month commit or 25% if we commit 750k/mo. try for 6mo opt-out w/ onboarding waived. i'll draft the email and loop legal after vendor confirms SOC2/DPA.
Alex K: timeline: want to start pilot by 2026-04-10. james, can you confirm integration ETA if vendor provides keys + sample logs by next Thu?
James P: yes — approx 2 weeks to integrate and validate with sample data.
Maria P: i'll open the procurement ticket now and ping vendor. assigning to @Elaine (Fin) for final sign-off and @James P for integration SLA. will post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
Elaine (Fin): approved pending the items above (SOC2, PO/net-30, onboarding credit). once procurement ticket is created, i'll push PO through.
Alex K: awesome — thanks all. i'll post vendor responses as they come.
Maria P: created ticket PR-2026-119 in procurement queue. next steps: vendor confirms SOC2 + billing entity, we negotiate 6mo pilot + onboarding waiver, finance issues PO.
James P: noted. i'll plan for a feature-flagged rollout and smoke tests during integration window.
Alex K: closing loop: if vendor pushes back on 6mo, we can fallback to 9mo with a slightly better discount. Maria — keep me posted on final negotiated T&Cs.
Maria P: will do.
